title: A very long light trip
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: In an expanding universe, distances between widely separated galaxies can change while light is traveling. The present distance is therefore not always the travel time multiplied by light speed.

misconception: A learner may choose: No: all cosmic distances are fixed during the trip
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Can the current distance to a very distant galaxy exceed the time its light traveled multiplied by the speed of light?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Can the current distance to a very distant galaxy exceed the time its light traveled multiplied by the speed of light? Yes: cosmic expansion changes distances during the trip. In an expanding universe, distances between widely separated galaxies can change while light is traveling. The present distance is therefore not always the travel time multiplied by light speed.
Visual caption: Distance changes en route. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: Can the current distance to a very distant galaxy exceed the time its light traveled multiplied by the speed of light?
options: Only if light traveled faster than light
Yes: cosmic expansion changes distances during the trip
No: all cosmic distances are fixed during the trip
recall.why: In an expanding universe, distances between widely separated galaxies can change while light is traveling. The present distance is therefore not always the travel time multiplied by light speed.
